Student Study Guidelines
Document Type: Guideline
Effective Date: January 1, 2026
Purpose
This guideline provides recommendations to help students develop effective study habits, manage 
their time efficiently, and achieve academic success. While these guidelines are not mandatory 
rules, students are strongly encouraged to follow them throughout their studies.
Study Preparation
Students are encouraged to:
•
Attend all scheduled classes and arrive on time.
•
Review lecture materials before and after each class.
•
Organize notes and learning materials by subject.
•
Prepare the required textbooks, stationery, and learning resources before each lesson.
Time Management
Effective time management helps students balance academic and personal responsibilities. Students 
should:
•
Create a weekly study schedule.
•
Set realistic academic goals.
•
Complete assignments well before their deadlines.
•
Allocate sufficient time for revision before examinations.
•
Avoid procrastination by studying regularly instead of cramming.
Classroom Participation
Students are encouraged to:
•
Participate actively in classroom discussions.
•
Ask questions when clarification is needed.
•
Work collaboratively during group activities.
•
Respect different opinions and learning styles.
Independent Learning
Students should develop lifelong learning habits by:

•
Reading additional reference materials.
•
Using the library and online academic resources.
•
Practicing problem-solving and critical thinking.
•
Reviewing feedback provided by lecturers to improve future work.
Digital Learning
When using online learning platforms, students should:
•
Log in regularly to check announcements and course materials.
•
Submit assignments through the designated platform before the deadline.
•
Participate respectfully in online discussions.
•
Maintain the confidentiality of their login credentials.
Examination Preparation
To prepare effectively for examinations, students are advised to:
•
Review course materials throughout the semester.
•
Practice using previous examination questions where available.
•
Form study groups to discuss difficult topics.
•
Ensure adequate rest before examination day.
•
Arrive at the examination venue early with all required materials.
Seeking Academic Support
Students who experience academic difficulties are encouraged to seek assistance from:
•
Course lecturers
•
Academic advisors
•
Library staff
•
Student support services
•
Peer tutoring or study groups
Seeking help early can improve learning outcomes and reduce academic stress.
Healthy Study Habits
Students should maintain a healthy lifestyle by:
•
Getting sufficient sleep each night.
•
Eating balanced meals.

•
Taking regular breaks during study sessions.
•
Exercising regularly.
•
Managing stress through healthy activities and seeking support when needed.
Review
These guidelines may be reviewed periodically to ensure they remain relevant and continue to 
support student success.
